rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no disagreement that a man may own two sisters together, or a mother and her daughter.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف في جواز جمعهما في الملك، وكذلك الأم وبنتها

rows.speaker: إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya infers from Ishaq's position that a man who has intercourse with both sisters would be stoned.
rows.anchor: ويجيء من قول إسحاق أن يرجم الجامع بينهما بالوطء

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik's ruling suspending a man after intercourse with both sisters implies disapproval; he imposed no fixed penalty.
rows.anchor: وتستقرأ الكراهية من قول مالك: إنه إذا وطئ واحدة ثم وطئ أخرى وقف عنهما

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وابن عمر والحسن البصري والأوزاعي والشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق
rows.claim: These authorities forbid intercourse with the second sister until the first is removed from ownership by sale, emancipation, or marriage.
rows.anchor: فقال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه وابن عمر والحسن البصري والأوزاعي والشافعي وأحمد وإسحاق: لا يجوز له وطء الثانية

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada's alternative permits intercourse with the second after the man intends to forbid himself the first, abstains, and completes her waiting period.
rows.anchor: وهو أنه إن كان يطأ واحدة وأراد وطء الأخرى فإنه ينوي تحريم الأولى على نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Malik's school, an owner may have intercourse with either sister, while restraint from the other is initially entrusted to his honesty.
rows.anchor: فله أن يطأ أيتهما شاء، والكف عن الأخرى موكول إلى أمانته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To switch sisters under Malik's rule, he must prohibit himself from the first through disposal, marriage, emancipation for a term, or long-term service.
rows.anchor: فإن أراد وطء الأخرى فيلزمه أن يحرم على نفسه فرج الأولى بفعل يفعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If he has intercourse with one and then unexpectedly with the other, both are suspended until he prohibits one, because he is now suspect.
rows.anchor: وقف عنهما ولم يجز له قرب إحداهما حتى يحرم الأخرى، ولم يبق ذلك إلى أمانته

rows.speaker: المدونة
rows.claim: One Maliki position suspends both women when he contracts marriage to the slave sister, disliking a contract made where intercourse is forbidden except for a common temporary impediment such as menstruation.
rows.anchor: في النكاح الثالث من المدونة أنه يوقف عنهما إذا وقع عقد النكاح

rows.speaker: قول آخر
rows.claim: Another position holds that the marriage contract does not take effect.
rows.anchor: وفي الباب بعينه قول آخر: إن النكاح لا ينعقد

rows.speaker: أشهب
rows.claim: Ashhab says contracting marriage to one sister itself prohibits intercourse with the enslaved sister.
rows.anchor: عقد النكاح في الواحدة تحريم لفرج المملوكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet forbade combining a woman with her paternal or maternal aunt, and the community reached consensus on this prohibition.
rows.anchor: وثبت عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه نهى أن يجمع بين المرأة وعمتها، وبين المرأة وخالتها، وأجمعت الأمة على ذلك

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars considered the aunt-and-niece prohibition hadith to abrogate the general permission in 4:24.
rows.anchor: وقد رأى بعض العلماء أن هذا الحديث ناسخ لعموم قوله تعالى: وأحل لكم ما وراء ذلكم

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari reads the opening negation as rejecting the preceding claim that the speakers believed the revelation, then begins a fresh oath that they do not believe.
rows.anchor: قوله: فلا رد على ما تقدم، تقديره: فليس الأمر كما يزعمون أنهم آمنوا بما أنزل إليك

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another explanation places the first lā before the oath to stress the negation; repeating it confirms the emphasis, and either lā could be omitted with a different effect.
rows.anchor: إنما قدم «لا» على القسم اهتماما بالنفي، وإظهارا لقوته، ثم كررها بعده تأكيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shajara means that their affairs became entangled, by analogy with the interlacing of tree branches; shajir likewise describes affection mixed with a friend's.
rows.anchor: وشجر معناه: اختلط والتف من أمورهم، وهو من الشجر، شبيه بالتفاف الأغصان

rows.speaker: أبو السمال
rows.claim: Abu al-Sammal reads shajara with a still jīm.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال «شجر» بإسكان الجيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya thinks Abu al-Sammal avoided successive vowel movements, but judges the reading weak because fatḥa is light.
rows.anchor: وأظنه فر من توالي الحركات، وليس بالقوي، لخفة الفتحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaḥakkimūka is subjunctive after ḥattā, which here marks a bare endpoint; yajidū is coordinated with it.
rows.anchor: ويحكموك نصب بحتى، لأنها هاهنا غاية مجردة، ويجدوا عطف عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haraj means constriction, burden, and hardship.
rows.anchor: والحرج: الضيق والتكلف والمشقة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets haraj as doubt.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: حرجا، شكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taslīman is an emphatic verbal noun indicating genuine submission; Arabs append a verbal noun when an action truly occurred, as in 4:164, though it can also exaggerate an unreal action, as in the cited poem.
rows.anchor: وقوله: تسليما مصدر مؤكد، منبىء على التحقيق في التسليم

rows.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
rows.claim: Mujahid and others say the verse concerns the previously mentioned people who sought judgment from the false deity; al-Tabari prefers this because it best fits the sequence.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وغيره: المراد بهذه الآية من تقدم ذكره، ممن أراد التحاكم إلى الطاغوت

rows.speaker: طائفة
rows.claim: Another group says the verse came after a dispute between al-Zubayr and a man over irrigation: the Prophet first ordered water passed to the neighbor, then gave al-Zubayr his full right after the man objected.
rows.anchor: نزلت في رجل خاصم الزبير بن العوام في السقي بماء الحرة، فقال لهما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some who report the al-Zubayr occasion identify the disputant as an Anṣārī who fought at Badr.
rows.anchor: فقال قوم: هو رجل من الأنصار من أهل بدر

rows.speaker: مكي وغيره
rows.claim: Makki and others identify the disputant as Ḥāṭib ibn Abī Baltaʿa.
rows.anchor: وقال مكي وغيره: هو حاطب بن أبي بلتعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the authentic Bukhari account identifies the disputant as an Anṣārī; al-Zubayr thought the verse was revealed about this incident.
rows.anchor: والصحيح الذي وقع في البخاري أنه رجل من الأنصار، وأن الزبير قال: فما أحسب أن هذه الآية نزلت إلا في ذلك

rows.speaker: طائفة
rows.claim: Another group says the verse followed ʿUmar's killing of a hypocrite who rejected the Prophet's judgment; the Prophet objected, and the revelation denied the man's faith and vindicated ʿUmar.
rows.anchor: لما قتل عمر الرجل المنافق الذي لم يرض بحكم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، بلغ ذلك النبي وعظم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Katabnā means We prescribed, while kill yourselves means that some of you kill others; Ibn ʿAṭiyya points to a parallel in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: وكتبنا معناه فرضنا، واقتلوا أنفسكم معناه ليقتل بعضكم بعضا، وقد تقدم نظيره في البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nūn of an and the wāw of aw may each be read with ḍamma or kasra; Ibn ʿĀmir, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr, and al-Kisāʾī use ḍamma, while Ḥamza and ʿĀṣim use kasra, and Abū ʿAmr combines kasra on nūn with ḍamma on wāw.
rows.anchor: وضم النون من أن وكسرها جائز، وكذلك الواو من أو اخرجوا وبضمها قرأ ابن عامر ونافع وابن كثير والكسائي

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir alone reads qalīlan in the accusative; Ibn ʿAṭiyya allows this by treating negation like affirmation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحده بالنصب «إلا قليلا» ، وذلك جائز أجرى النفي مجرى الإيجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qalīl is nominative as an appositive to the pronoun in faʿalūhu.
rows.anchor: وقليل رفع على البدل من الضمير في فعلوه

rows.speaker: حكاية
rows.claim: The reported occasion has Jews mock hypocrites for following Muhammad but rejecting his judgment, contrasting this with their own obedience to a command to kill themselves, in which seventy thousand died; Thābit ibn Qays said they would obey if prescribed.
rows.anchor: أن اليهود قالوا لما لم يرض المنافق بحكم النبي عليه السلام: ما رأينا أسخف من هؤلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that account, the verse teaches that the hypocrites would not obey such a command and that only a few sincere believers, such as Thābit, would.
rows.anchor: فنزلت الآية معلمة حال أولئك المنافقين، وأنه لو كتب ذلك على الأمة لم يفعلوه

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet names Thābit ibn Qays, ʿAmmār, and Ibn Masʿūd among the few who would obey.
rows.anchor: وكذلك روي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: ثابت بن قيس وعمار وابن مسعود من القليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in minhum includes both hypocrites and believers because both shared the outward community and practices of Islam.
rows.anchor: وشركهم في ضمير منهم لما كان المنافقون والمؤمنون مشتركين في دعوة الإسلام وظواهر الشريعة

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق السبيعي
rows.claim: Abu Isḥāq al-Sabīʿī recounts that after the verse descended, a man said he would obey if commanded and thanked God for sparing them; the Prophet then praised believers whose faith was firmer than mountains.
rows.anchor: لما نزلت ولو أنا كتبنا عليهم الآية، قال رجل: لو أمرنا لفعلنا، والحمد لله الذي عافانا

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makki identifies the man in Abu Isḥāq's report as Abū Bakr.
rows.anchor: وذكر مكي أن الرجل هو أبو بكر الصديق

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqāsh identifies that man as ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.
rows.anchor: وذكر النقاش: أنه عمر بن الخطاب

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: Abū Bakr reportedly said that, if the command had been prescribed, he would have begun with himself and his family.
rows.anchor: وذكر عن أبي بكر أنه قال: لو كتب علينا لبدأت بنفسي وبأهل بيتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If these hypocrites had acted on the admonition, they would have taken heed and repented.
rows.anchor: ولو أنهم فعلوا أي لو أن هؤلاء المنافقين اتعظوا وأنابوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tathbīt means certainty, affirmation, and related senses: God would make them steadfast.
rows.anchor: وتثبيتا معناه: يقينا وتصديقا ونحو هذا، أي يثبتهم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description of the reward as immense implies a lasting bliss beyond what any human can attain or comprehend.
rows.anchor: ووصفه إياه بالعظم مقتض ما لا يحصله بشر من النعيم المقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is faith that leads to Paradise.
rows.anchor: و «الصراط المستقيم» : الإيمان المؤدي إلى الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although reward is mentioned before guidance, guidance necessarily precedes reward; the order lists divine favors rather than chronology.
rows.anchor: ومعلوم أن الهداية قبل إعطاء الأجر، لأن المقصد إنما هو تعديد ما كان الله ينعم به عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the blessing for obeying, God gives the reward of those who do obey.
rows.anchor: لما ذكر الله الأمر الذي لو فعلوه لأنعم عليهم، ذكر بعد ذلك ثواب من يفعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya reads this verse as an explanation of the prayer for the straight path and the path of those blessed, cited as al-Fātiḥa 1:5.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية تفسير قوله تعالى: اهدنا الصراط المستقيم صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم

rows.speaker: طائفة
rows.claim: A group says the verse came after ʿAbd Allāh ibn Zayd ibn ʿAbd Rabbih, who had been shown the call to prayer, grieved that he might not meet the Prophet in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: لما قال عبد الله بن زيد بن عبد ربه الأنصاري الذي أري الأذان، يا رسول الله إذا مت ومتنا كنت في عليين فلا نراك

rows.speaker: مكي
rows.claim: Makki says that after the Prophet died, ʿAbd Allāh prayed to be blinded so he would see nothing after him, and became blind; a group of Anṣār said similar things, according to Ibn Jubayr, Qatada, and al-Suddī.
rows.anchor: أنه لما مات النبي عليه السلام، قال اللهم أعمني حتى لا أرى شيئا بعده، فعمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being with the blessed means sharing one abode and enjoyment, each person content and not feeling inferior, although Paradise's ranks differ by deeds and God's favor.
rows.anchor: أنهم في دار واحدة، ومتنعم واحد، وكل من فيها قد رزق الرضا بحاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣiddīq may derive from truthfulness or from charity.
rows.anchor: و «الصديق» فعيل من الصدق، وقيل من الصدقة

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says that ṣiddīqūn are those who give charity; martyrs are those killed in God's path, specially honored in death and exempt from washing and funeral prayer.
rows.anchor: وروي عن النبي عليه السلام، الصديقون المتصدقون، والشهداء المقتولون في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: قول
rows.claim: Martyrs are so called either because God testified that they would enter Paradise or because they testified to the truth for God in pursuit of His pleasure at death.
rows.anchor: وسموا بذلك لأن الله شهد لهم بالجنة، وقيل لأنهم شهدوا لله بالحق في موتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this verse, the word martyrs encompasses all kinds of martyrs.
rows.anchor: ولكن لفظ، الشهداء في هذه الآية يعم أنواع الشهداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rafīqan is singular in form but collective in meaning, as in 22:5; it is accusative of specification, or circumstantial, with the first analysis preferred.
rows.anchor: ورفيقا موحد في معنى الجمع، كما قال: ثم يخرجكم طفلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rafīqan is best parsed as accusative of specification, though it has also been analyzed as a circumstantial accusative.
rows.anchor: ونصبه على التمييز، وقيل على الحال، والأول أصوب

rows.speaker: أبو السمال
rows.claim: Abu al-Sammal reads ḥasuna with a still sīn, as in the word shajara.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو السمال، «وحسن» بسكون السين، وذلك مثل شجر بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That favor answers a hypothetical objection that obedience cannot make people equal to prophets in the afterlife when their earthly ranks differ: companionship is by God's favor, not an obligation on Him.
rows.anchor: ذلك الفضل من الله رد على تقدير معترض يقول، وما الذي يوجب استواء أهل الطاعة والنبيين في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not establish equal rank: the obedient share the blessed one's abode while their stations remain distinct.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فلا نقرر الاستواء، بل هم معهم في دار والمنازل متباينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing phrase tells people to submit to God's favor without objection and rely on His knowledge; the added bāʾ signals this directive.
rows.anchor: فسلموا فعل الله وتفضله من الاعتراض عليه، واكتفوا بعلمه في ذلك وغيره

none: A continuation fragment and bare heading only; no distinct point.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised burhān is Muḥammad, a clear, luminous proof from God establishing the truth of his call and the error of other creeds.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى محمد رسول الله، و «البرهان» : الحجة النيرة الواضحة التي تعطي اليقين التام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The manifest light is the Qur'an, which explains everything and admonishes, restrains, forbids, and commands.
rows.anchor: يعني القرآن فيه بيان لكل شيء، وهو الواعظ الزاجر، الناهي الآمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in bihi can refer either to God or to the Qur'an just mentioned as manifest light.
rows.anchor: والضمير في به يحتمل أن يعود على الله تعالى، ويحتمل أن يعود على القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʿtiṣām means holding fast to it and seeking protection and salvation through it, as one is protected by fortresses.
rows.anchor: به التمسك بسببه وطلب النجاة والمنعة به

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: The Prophet describes the Qur'an as God's firm rope and says that whoever holds to it is protected.
rows.anchor: القرآن حبل الله المتين من تمسك به عصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mercy and bounty mean Paradise and its delights.
rows.anchor: و «الرحمة» و «الفضل» : الجنة وتنعيمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yahdīhim means guiding them to the bounty, along the road to the gardens; this is route guidance, since guidance of instruction had already occurred through faith and adherence to the Book.
rows.anchor: ويهديهم، معناه: إلى الفضل، وهذه هداية طريق الجنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised route guidance is illustrated by 47:5, and the believers had already received guidance of instruction when they believed and held to God's Book.
rows.anchor: كما قال تعالى: سيهديهم ويصلح بالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sirāṭan may be governed by an implied verb indicated by yahdīhim, function as a second object, or be parsed adverbially or circumstantially; the path itself means a road as explained earlier.
rows.anchor: وصراطا نصب بإضمار فعل يدل عليه يهديهم، تقديره فيعرفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chapter is Medinan by consensus.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة مدنية بإجماع

rows.speaker: أبو سلمة
rows.claim: A report cited by al-Naqqāsh says the chapter was revealed as the Prophet returned from al-Ḥudaybiyya; he told ʿAlī that al-Māʾida had descended and was a blessed benefit.
rows.anchor: وذكر النقاش عن أبي سلمة أنه قال: لما رجع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من الحديبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the reported wording does not sound like something the Prophet would say.
rows.anchor: وهذا عندي لا يشبه كلام النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some passages came during the Farewell Pilgrimage and others in the year of the Conquest, including the clause about a people's hatred after they barred access to the Sacred Mosque.
rows.anchor: ومنها ما نزل عام الفتح وهو قوله تعالى: ولا يجرمنكم شنآن قوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anything revealed after the Hijra is classified as Medinan, whether revealed in Medina, on a journey, or in Mecca; Meccan refers to revelation before the migration.
rows.anchor: وكل ما نزل من القرآن بعد هجرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فهو مدني سواء ما نزل بالمدينة أو في سفر

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report says al-Māʾida is called the saving chapter in the heavenly realm and rescues its companion from the angels of punishment.
rows.anchor: سورة المائدة تدعى في ملكوت الله المنقذة تنقذ صاحبها من أيدي ملائكة العذاب

rows.speaker: علقمة
rows.claim: ʿAlqama says every Qur'anic address beginning “O you who believe” is Medinan.
rows.anchor: قال علقمة: كل ما في القرآن يا أيها الذين آمنوا فهو مدني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wafā and awfā have the same meaning.
rows.anchor: ويقال: وفى وأوفى بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands all believers to honor covenants, meaning spoken commitments such as an agreement for good, marriage, or sale.
rows.anchor: وأمر الله تعالى المؤمنين عامة بالوفاء بالعقود. وهي الربوط في القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers includes sincere believers and People of the Book, who have a covenant with God to honor what their scriptures say about Muḥammad.
rows.anchor: ولفظ المؤمنين يعم مؤمني أهل الكتاب. إذ بينهم وبين الله عقد في أداء الأمانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Covenants include pre-Islamic agreements grounded in justice, such as preventing oppression; Islam voided agreements for oppression and raids, so only commitments consistent with religious law must be honored.
rows.anchor: ولفظ «العقود» يعم عقود الجاهلية المبنية على بر مثل دفع الظلم ونحوه

rows.speaker: الناس
rows.claim: Commentators commonly gloss al-ʿuqūd as covenants.
rows.anchor: وفسر الناس لفظ «العقود» بالعهود

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada interprets the command as honoring pre-Islamic covenants; a report from the Prophet says to fulfill such a pact and not form a new pact in Islam.
rows.anchor: قول قتادة (أوفوا بالعقود) معناه بعهد الجاهلية. روي لنا عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported instruction concerns private pacts in the pre-Islamic community; Islam bound all believers as brothers, so private arrangements for exclusive future advantage do not stand, while joint promises to resist an actual injustice remain binding.
rows.anchor: أن عقد الجاهلية كان يخص المتعاقدين، إذ كان الجمهور على ظلم وضلال، والإسلام قد ربط الجميع

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari cites Furat ibn Ḥayyān asking the Prophet about a pre-Islamic alliance; the Prophet identifies the alliance of Lujaym and Taym Allāh and says Islam only strengthens it.
rows.anchor: وذكر أن فرات بن حيان العجلي سأل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن حلف الجاهلية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets fulfilling covenants as observing everything God made lawful, unlawful, obligatory, or prescribed in all matters; Mujahid and others agree.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنه أوفوا بالعقود معناه بما أحل الله وبما حرم وبما فرض

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي وابن زيد وغيرهما
rows.claim: These authorities take al-ʿuqūd to mean every commitment a person binds himself to, including sale and marriage.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن كعب القرظي وابن زيد وغيرهما «العقود» في الآية هي كل ما ربطه المرء على نفسه

rows.speaker: ابن زيد وعبد الله بن عبيدة
rows.claim: They list five covenants: faith, marriage, pledge, sale, and oath.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد وعبد الله بن عبيدة: العقود خمس: عقدة الإيمان وعقدة النكاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the covenant categories can be reduced to fewer than five.
rows.anchor: وقد تنحصر إلى أقل من خمس

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj understands the verse as the covenants God took from the People of the Book to act on their revealed scripture.
rows.anchor: هي العقود التي أخذها الله على أهل الكتاب أن يعملوا بما جاءهم

rows.speaker: ابن شهاب
rows.claim: Ibn Shihab says the Prophet's letter to ʿAmr ibn Ḥazm, sent to Najran, opened with this command and included verses through 5:4.
rows.anchor: قرأت كتاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الذي كتب لعمرو بن حزم حين بعثه إلى نجران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best interpretation generalizes both terms: believers includes anyone outwardly professing faith and true believers, while covenants are every verbal commitment consistent with truth and religious law.
rows.anchor: وأصوب ما يقال في تفسير هذه الآية أن تعمم ألفاظها بغاية ما تتناول

rows.speaker: الحطيئة
rows.claim: Al-Ḥuṭayʾa's verse uses ʿaqadū to illustrate the word for making a covenant.
rows.anchor: قول الحطيئة: قوم إذا عقدوا عقدا لجارهم ... شدوا العناج وشدوا فوقه الكربا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lawfulness of livestock addresses those who fully embrace faith and overturns Arab customs that had forbidden certain categories such as the saʾiba, baḥīra, and ḥāmī.
rows.anchor: وكانت للعرب سنن في «الأنعام» من السائبة والبحيرة والحام وغير ذلك فنزلت هذه الآية رافعة لجميع ذلك

rows.speaker: السدي والربيع وقتادة والضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Suddī, al-Rabīʿ, Qatada, and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say bahīmat al-anʿām means all livestock; Ibn ʿAṭiyya explains it as naming the genus through its most specific subset.
rows.anchor: فقال السدي والربيع وقتادة والضحاك: هي «الأنعام» كلها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan defines bahīmat al-anʿām as camels, cattle, and sheep.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: بهيمة الأنعام الإبل والبقر والغنم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says the phrase includes fetuses delivered when their mothers are slaughtered, which may be eaten without a separate slaughter.
rows.anchor: وروي عن عبد الله بن عمر أنه قال بهيمة الأنعام الأجنة التي تخرج عند الذبح للأمهات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also includes these fetuses among bahīmat al-anʿām.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هذه الأجنة من بهيمة الأنعام

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some commentators, including a report from al-Ḍaḥḥāk outside al-Tabari, take bahīmat al-anʿām to mean wild livestock such as gazelles, wild cattle, and asses.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم بهيمة الأنعام وحشها كالظباء وبقر الوحش والحمر وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cited, unattributed line uses ḥarām for one in consecration; the gloss mulabb means responding to the pilgrimage call.
rows.anchor: فقلت لها فيئي إليك فإنني ... حرام وإني بعد ذاك لبيب أي ملب

rows.speaker: الحسن وإبراهيم ويحيى بن وثاب
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Ibrāhīm, and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read ḥurum with a still rāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وإبراهيم ويحيى بن وثاب «حرم» بسكون الراء

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan calls the still-vowel reading a Tamīmī dialect that similarly suppresses vowels in words such as rusul and kutub.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الحسن هذه لغة تميمية يقولون في رسل رسل وفي كتب كتب ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God decrees as He wills reinforces laws that differ from Arab custom: the Lord of all may decree without anyone overruling Him.
rows.anchor: تقوية لهذه الأحكام الشرعية المخالفة لمعهود أحكام العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is exceptionally eloquent and dense, combining five rulings: honor covenants, permit livestock, except what follows, except game during consecration, and permit hunting to those outside consecration.
rows.anchor: فإنها تضمنت خمسة أحكام: الأمر بالوفاء بالعقود وتحليل بهيمة الأنعام

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqāsh tells how al-Kindī's companions challenged him to imitate the Qur'an; after trying, he conceded that the opening of al-Māʾida compresses commands, prohibitions, layered exceptions, and divine power and wisdom beyond human ability.
rows.anchor: وحكى النقاش أن أصحاب الكندي قالوا للكندي: أيها الحكيم اعمل لنا مثل هذا القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on dissolving God's rites addresses true believers and means not transgressing God's limits in any matter; shaʿāʾir are signs or landmarks God marks as His boundaries and obedience.
rows.anchor: خطاب للمؤمنين حقا أن لا يتعدوا حدود الله في أمر من الأمور

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī interprets God's rites as His sacred limits.
rows.anchor: فقال السدي شعائر الله حرم الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets the rites as pilgrimage ceremonies; Muslims wanted to attack pagans who performed pilgrimage, umra, and sacrifice, so the verse forbade this.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس شعائر الله مناسك الحج. وكان المشركون يحجون ويعتمرون ويهدون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also says the rites are all that consecration makes forbidden.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا شعائر الله ما حد تحريمه في الإحرام

rows.speaker: عطاء بن أبي رباح
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ ibn Abī Rabāḥ says the rites include everything God commands or forbids; Ibn ʿAṭiyya identifies this as the strongest view.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء بن أبي رباح، شعائر الله جميع ما أمر به أو نهى عنه، وهذا هو القول الراجح

rows.speaker: ابن الكلبي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Kalbī says the verse addressed Arabs who did not count Ṣafā and Marwa as rites and Quraysh, who did not stand at ʿArafāt.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الكلبي كان عامة العرب لا يعدون الصفا والمروة من الشعائر وكانت قريش لا تقف بعرفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular sacred month represents all sacred months; the Prophet names Dhū al-Qaʿda, Dhū al-Ḥijja, Muḥarram, and Rajab of Muḍar between Jumādā and Shaʿbān.
rows.anchor: اسم مفرد يدل على الجنس في جميع الأشهر الحرم وهي كما قال النبي عليه السلام ذو القعدة وذو الحجة والمحرم ورجب مضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rajab is attributed to Muḍar because they especially honored it; they laid down arms and removed spearheads, calling it the month of unhearing because weapons were silent.
rows.anchor: وإنما أضيف إلى مضر لأنها كانت تختص بتحريمه. وتزيل فيه السلاح، وتنزع الأسنة من الرماح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs agreed on three sacred months, but the long truce led to nasiʾ: they would declare Muḥarram lawful and make Ṣafar sacred instead, which God prohibited here and in 9:37.
rows.anchor: فلذلك اتخذت النسيء وهو أن يحل لها ذلك المتكلم نعيم بن ثعلبة وغيره المحرم يحرم بدله صفرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muḥarram became the year's first month because pilgrimage completed the year's purpose and harvest, after which a new year began; ʿUmar accordingly dated the registers from it.
rows.anchor: وجعل المحرم أول شهور السنة من حيث كان الحج والموسم غاية العام وثمرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban means not to violate the sacred month by fighting, raiding, or altering its status, since changing it amounts to permitting what is sacred.
rows.anchor: أي لا تحلوه بقتال ولا غارة ولا تبديل فإن تبديله استحلال لحرمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya's preferred reading is that the sacred month here is Rajab, whose status God emphasizes because Arabs were not unanimous about it.
rows.anchor: والأظهر عندي أن الشهر الحرام أريد به رجب ليشتد أمره

rows.speaker: عوف بن الأحوص
rows.claim: ʿAwf ibn al-Aḥwaṣ's verse refers to the month of Banū Umayya and sacrificial offerings while blood is being shed; Abū ʿUbayda identifies this as Rajab.
rows.anchor: قول عوف بن الأحوص: وشهر بني أمية والهدايا ... إذا حبست مضرجها الدماء

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says the poet means Rajab, revered by Quraysh's elders; al-Akhfash notes this in al-Mufaḍḍaliyyāt, and al-Tabari also identifies Rajab of Muḍar.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة أراد رجبا لأنه شهر كانت مشايخ قريش تعظمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya's rationale for specifying Rajab is that God intensified the status of a month the Arabs did not unanimously honor.
rows.anchor: فوجه هذا التخصيص هو كما قد ذكرت أن الله تعالى شدد أمر هذا الشهر

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says the sacred month is Dhū al-Qaʿda because it is the first of the sacred months; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls “first” approximate since the months rotate and sequence depends on a contextual occasion.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: المراد في هذه الآية ذو القعدة من حيث كان أولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no disagreement that hady means livestock dedicated as an offering to the House for worship, which must not be seized or plundered.
rows.anchor: أما الهدي فلا خلاف أنه ما أهدي من النعم إلى بيت الله وقصدت به القربة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is reported to say that the garlands are the garlanded sacrifices, while an offering is called hady before being garlanded.
rows.anchor: فحكى الطبري عن ابن عباس أن القلائد هي الهدي المقلد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says al-Tabari overreads Ibn ʿAbbās: the statement does not limit hady to ungarlanded offerings; the garlanded portion is repeated for emphasis.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي قال الطبري تحامل على ألفاظ ابن عباس وليس يلزم من كلام ابن عباس أن الهدي إنما يقال لما لم يقلد

rows.speaker: جمهور الناس
rows.claim: The majority say hady includes all offerings dedicated as worship and qalaʾid are the protective garlands people wore.
rows.anchor: وقال جمهور الناس: الهدي عام في أنواع ما أهدي قربة والقلائد ما كان الناس يتقلدونه أمنة لهم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says a pagan pilgrim wore a garland of acacia bark when setting out for pilgrimage as a sign of consecration and pilgrimage, protecting him from harm.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: كان الرجل في الجاهلية إذا خرج يريد الحج تقلد من السمر قلادة فلم يعرض له أحد بسوء

rows.speaker: عطاء وغيره
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and others say people leaving the sanctuary for errands wore bark from its trees to show they belonged to the sanctuary or were pilgrims, and God forbade violating anyone protected by such signs.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء وغيره: بل كان الناس إذا خرجوا من الحرم في حوائج لهم تقلدوا من شجر الحرم ومن لحائه
